source_title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
evidence_excerpt: Headline CPI inflation increased to 6.7 per cent during July-August 2020 as pressures accentuated across food, fuel and core constituents on account of supply disruptions, higher margins and taxes.
ambiguity_or_context_note: Value is stated for a combined two-month period; no standalone latest-month level is assigned.

source_title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting December 2 to 4, 2020
evidence_excerpt: CPI inflation rose sharply to 7.3 per cent in September and further to 7.6 per cent in October 2020, with some evidence that price pressures are spreading.

source_title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 3-5, 2021
evidence_excerpt: After breaching the upper tolerance threshold of 6 per cent for six consecutive months (June-November 2020), CPI inflation fell to 4.6 per cent in December on the back of easing food prices and favourable base effects.

source_title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 5-7, 2021
evidence_excerpt: Headline inflation increased to 5.0 per cent in February after having eased to 4.1 per cent in January 2021.

source_title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, June 2 to 4, 2021
evidence_excerpt: Headline inflation registered a moderation to 4.3 per cent in April from 5.5 per cent in March, largely on favourable base effects.
ambiguity_or_context_note: Reference year inferred from past-month narrative and decision-year context.

source_title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, August 4 to 6, 2021
evidence_excerpt: Headline CPI inflation plateaued at 6.3 per cent in June after having risen by 207 basis points in May 2021.

source_title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, October 6 to 8, 2021
evidence_excerpt: Headline CPI inflation at 5.3 per cent in August softened for the second consecutive month, declining by one percentage point from the recent peak in May-June 2021.

source_title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, December 6 to 8, 2021
evidence_excerpt: Headline CPI inflation, which has been on a downward trajectory since June 2021, edged up to 4.5 per cent in October from 4.3 per cent in September on account of a spike in vegetable prices – due to crop damage from heavy rainfalls in October in several states, and fuel inflation – driven up by international prices of liquefied petroleum gas and kerosene.

source_title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, February 8 to 10, 2022
evidence_excerpt: Headline CPI inflation edged up to 5.6 per cent y-o-y in December from 4.9 per cent in November due to large adverse base effects.
ambiguity_or_context_note: Reference year inferred from past-month narrative and decision-year context.

source_title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 6 to 8, 2022
evidence_excerpt: Headline CPI inflation edged up to 6.0 per cent in January 2022 and 6.1 per cent in February, breaching the upper tolerance threshold.

source_title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, May 2 and 4, 2022
evidence_excerpt: In March 2022, headline CPI inflation surged to 7.0 per cent from 6.1 per cent in February, largely reflecting the impact of geopolitical spillovers.

source_title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, June 6 to 8, 2022
evidence_excerpt: CPI headline inflation rose further from 7.0 per cent in March 2022 to 7.8 per cent in April 2022, reflecting broad-based increase in all its major constituents.

source_title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, August 3 to 5, 2022
evidence_excerpt: CPI inflation eased to 7.0 per cent (year-on-year, y-o-y) during May-June 2022 from 7.8 per cent in April, although it persists above the upper tolerance band.
additional_evidence_excerpt: Paragraph 18: The moderation seen in the headline inflation rate in May and June, from 7.8 per cent in April to 7.0 per cent was mainly on account of the decline in food inflation and inflation in the category of items excluding food and fuel & light.
ambiguity_or_context_note: Value is stated for a combined two-month period; no standalone latest-month level is assigned.

source_title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, September 28-30, 2022
evidence_excerpt: CPI inflation rose to 7.0 per cent (y-o-y) in August 2022 from 6.7 per cent in July as food inflation moved higher, driven by prices of cereals, vegetables, pulses, spices and milk.

source_title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, December 5-7, 2022
evidence_excerpt: CPI inflation moderated to 6.8 per cent (y-o-y) in October 2022 from 7.4 per cent in September, with favourable base effects mitigating the impact of pick-up in price momentum in October.

source_title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, February 6-8, 2023
evidence_excerpt: CPI headline inflation moderated to 5.7 per cent (y-o-y) in December 2022 – after easing to 5.9 per cent in November – on the back of double digit deflation in vegetable prices.

source_title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
evidence_excerpt: CPI headline inflation rose from 5.7 per cent in December 2022 to 6.4 per cent in February 2023 on the back of higher inflation in cereals, milk and fruits and slower deflation in vegetables prices.

source_title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, June 6 to 8, 2023
evidence_excerpt: CPI inflation fell sharply to 4.7 per cent in April 2023 from 6.4 per cent in February on the back of large favourable base effects, with softening observed across all the three major groups.

source_title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, August 8 to 10, 2023
evidence_excerpt: Headline CPI inflation picked up from 4.3 per cent in May to 4.8 per cent in June, driven largely by food group dynamics on the back of higher prices of vegetables, eggs, meat, fish, cereals, pulses and spices.
ambiguity_or_context_note: Reference year inferred from past-month narrative and decision-year context.

source_title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, October 4 to 6, 2023
evidence_excerpt: CPI headline inflation surged by 2.6 percentage points to 7.4 per cent in July due to spike in vegetable prices, before moderating somewhat in August to 6.8 per cent.

source_title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, December 6 to 8, 2023
evidence_excerpt: CPI headline inflation fell by about 2 percentage points since the last meeting of the MPC to 4.9 per cent in October 2023 on sharp correction in prices of certain vegetables, deflation in fuel and a broad-based moderation in core inflation (CPI inflation excluding food and fuel).

source_title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, February 6 to 8, 2024
evidence_excerpt: From its October 2023 trough of 4.9 per cent, CPI inflation increased successively in the next two months to 5.7 per cent by December.

source_title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3 to 5, 2024
evidence_excerpt: Headline inflation softened to 5.1 per cent during January-February 2024, from 5.7 per cent in December.
additional_evidence_excerpt: Paragraph 16: The annual headline inflation rate for February was 5.1 per cent the same level as in the previous month and well below 5.7 per cent in December 2023. | Paragraph 53: CPI headline inflation during January-February 2024 (5.1 per cent in each of the months) has moderated from the elevated level seen in December 2023 (5.7 per cent).
ambiguity_or_context_note: Resolution groups January-February; paragraphs 16 and 53 explicitly corroborate February at 5.1%.

source_title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, June 5 to 7, 2024
evidence_excerpt: Headline inflation has seen sequential moderation since February 2024, albeit in a narrow range from 5.1 per cent in February to 4.8 per cent in April 2024.

source_title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, August 6 to 8, 2024
evidence_excerpt: Headline inflation increased to 5.1 per cent in June 2024 after remaining steady at 4.8 per cent during April-May 2024.
